summary: This RFC defines RADIUS attributes for Proxy Mobile IPv6. The mobile access gateway and local mobility anchor use RADIUS interfaces with the AAA server for authentication, authorization, and policy.

plainLanguage.summary:
Proxy Mobile IPv6 lets the network move a mobile subscriber's session without the handset taking part in the hand-over. Two pieces of equipment do the work: the mobile access gateway at the edge of the visited network, and the local mobility anchor that owns the session in the home network.

Both need the subscriber's policy profile and address assignments, which live in the home network's authentication server. This RFC defines the RADIUS messages for fetching that information: the attributes the gateway sends and receives, the attributes the anchor sends and receives, and the capability bits that tell the two ends whether the session uses IPv4, IPv6 or both.

what does the mag send to the aaa server
subtitle: RADIUS attributes that let a mobility network fetch a subscriber's policy and addresses at attach time.

tldr.problem: Proxy Mobile IPv6 moves a mobile node's session in the network without the node taking part. The two boxes that do the work, the mobile access gateway and the local mobility anchor, still need the subscriber's policy and address assignments, and they get those from the home network's authentication server.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a RADIUS profile and eighteen new attributes for the two interfaces to that server, plus two new capability bits so the two ends can agree on whether IPv4, IPv6 or both are in use.
tldr.outcome: A Proxy Mobile IPv6 deployment can use its existing RADIUS infrastructure for policy retrieval, binding authorisation and accounting. RFC 8044 later updated this document.

today: RFC 6572 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, and it was later updated by RFC 8044, which defines the data types used in RADIUS attributes.

sections.title: What RADIUS Adds to Proxy Mobile IPv6
sections.content:
Proxy Mobile IPv6 is a network-based mobility management protocol that allows IP mobility support for a mobile node without requiring the mobile node's participation in any mobility-related signalling. The mobile management elements in the network, the mobile access gateway and the local mobility anchor, are the two key functions in this network-based mobility system. The mobile access gateway is responsible for detecting the mobile node's movements in the network and for initiating the needed mobility management signalling with the local mobility anchor. Both mobility management agents make use of the AAA infrastructure to retrieve the mobile node's policy profile and for performing service authorization.

This document defines a RADIUS-based profile and corresponding attributes to be used on the AAA interface between the mobile access gateway and the AAA RADIUS server. This interface is used to carry the per-mobile-node policy profile from the remote policy store to the mobile access gateway. The document also defines a RADIUS-based interface between the local mobility anchor and the AAA RADIUS server for authorization of the received Proxy Mobile IPv6 signalling messages. The procedures cover a mobile node connecting to the Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain from the home network and from a visited network.

The document also defines the baseline for the accounting generated by the mobile access gateway and the local mobility anchor.

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119. All the mobility-related terms used in the document are to be interpreted as defined in the Proxy Mobile IPv6 specifications and in RFC 5844. Four abbreviations are used. The Network Access Server provides authorization services for a device or user access to the network as defined in RADIUS; the document assumes that the NAS function is co-located with the mobile access gateway, and where they are decoupled the messaging interface between them is beyond the scope of the document. The Home AAA server is located in the mobile node's home network and has access to the mobile node's policy profiles. The Visited AAA server is located in the mobile node's visited network and takes the role of a proxy server, forwarding the received AAA service request to the Home AAA server and relaying the response after applying any local access network policies. The Local AAA is an AAA proxy located in the local network; in a roaming case the local AAA has the visited AAA role.
sections.plainLanguage: The gateway and the anchor both need to check with the home network before they let a subscriber roam. This RFC says exactly what those two conversations look like in RADIUS.

sections.title: The Solution and Its Deployment Models
sections.content:
The mobile node's policy profile is present in a policy store and is needed by the mobility management elements for authorizing the mobile node for mobility management service and for obtaining various service-related parameters. The policy store could be locally co-located with the mobility management agents, enabling direct local access, or it could be available from an AAA server through a RADIUS-based AAA interface.

When a mobile node attaches to an access network, the NAS on that access network may activate the network access authentication procedure. The choice of mechanism is specific to the access network deployment, but it is typically based on the Extensible Authentication Protocol. The NAS performs the network access authentication and queries the home AAA server using an AAA protocol such as RADIUS. If the authentication succeeds, the mobile node's policy profile is obtained as part of the RADIUS message exchange with the AAA server. The mobile node may be an IPv4-only node, an IPv6-only node or a dual-stack node, and based on the policy in the profile the network access authentication procedure SHOULD provide an unambiguous indication of the type of addresses to be assigned for the mobile node, together with all other service-related and policy parameters relevant to the mobility service.

After the successful network access authentication and the retrieval of the mobile node's policy profile, the mobile access gateway sends a Proxy Binding Update to the local mobility anchor. On receiving it, the anchor interacts with the home AAA server to obtain the mobile node's policy profile, which is required for authorizing and activating the mobility service.

The document adds support for three distinct use cases, taking into account the administrative domains to which the gateway and the anchor belong. In the first, both are in the home network, and both interact only with the home AAA server. In the second, both are in the visited network, and they exchange signalling with the home AAA server through the visited AAA server, which acts as a proxy; the visited network may append additional information to the home AAA replies to reflect local policy. In the third, the gateway is in the visited network while the anchor is in the home network, so any message between the gateway and the home AAA server passes through the visited AAA server acting as a proxy, while the anchor has direct access to the home AAA server.
sections.plainLanguage: The policy profile comes from the home network. Where the two pieces of equipment sit decides whether they reach it directly or through a proxy in the visited network. Three arrangements are possible, and the RFC supports all of them.

sections.title: The MIP6-Feature-Vector
sections.content:
The MIP6-Feature-Vector attribute, of type value 124, is of type OctetString and contains a 64-bit flags field of supported mobility capabilities. The document reserves two new capability bits according to the rules of RFC 5447 and reuses the Proxy Mobile IPv6 capability bits defined by RFC 5779.

PMIP6_SUPPORTED, with the value 0x0000010000000000, is used as defined in RFC 5779. IP4_HOA_SUPPORTED, with the value 0x0000020000000000, is also used as defined in RFC 5779, and assignment of the IPv4 home address is defined by RFC 5844. LOCAL_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED, with the value 0x0000040000000000, is used as defined in RFC 5779.

IP4_TRANSPORT_SUPPORTED, with the value 0x0000800000000000, is used for negotiation of IPv4 transport support between the gateway and the AAA server. When the gateway sets this flag bit, it indicates the ability to provide IPv4 transport, that is IPv4-based encapsulation, for carrying IP traffic between the gateway and the anchor. If the flag is unset in the returned attribute, the AAA server does not authorize the use of IPv4 transport on the gateway-to-anchor tunnel.

IP4_HOA_ONLY_SUPPORTED, with the value 0x0001000000000000, is used for determination of the authorized mobility mode. When the AAA server sets this bit, it indicates that Proxy Mobile IPv6 mobility with IPv4 support has only been authorized for the mobile node, and as a result the RADIUS Access-Accept SHOULD NOT carry the IPv6 Home Network Prefix. When this bit is set, the PMIP6_SUPPORTED flag MUST also be set and the IP4_HOA_SUPPORTED flag MUST NOT be set.

The combinations mean: the PMIP6-SUPPORTED bit set on its own means only IPv6 mobility is supported and authorized; PMIP6_SUPPORTED and IP4-ONLY-HOA-SUPPORTED together mean only IPv4 mobility is supported and authorized; PMIP6_SUPPORTED and IP4-HOA-SUPPORTED together mean both IPv6 and IPv4 mobility are supported and authorized.

The attribute is also used on the anchor to the AAA server interface, where it enables direct capability negotiation between the anchor and the AAA server, and the capabilities announced by both parties are known to be mutually supported. The anchor may use this mechanism during authorization of a received Proxy Binding Update against the AAA server to check individual feature permissions for a particular mobile node. If the RADIUS Access-Accept contains a contradicting combination of the capability flag bits, such as both the IP4_HOA_ONLY_SUPPORTED and the IP4_HOA_SUPPORTED flags being set, then the RADIUS client MUST treat the Access-Accept as an Access-Reject and SHOULD log the event. Similarly, if the Access-Request contains a contradicting combination, the RADIUS server MUST reply with an Access-Reject message and SHOULD log the event.
sections.plainLanguage: A 64-bit field of flags says what the network can do: IPv6 mobility, IPv4 home address, local routing, IPv4 transport. The two ends compare flags, and if the home network returns a contradictory combination the session is refused rather than half set up.

sections.title: Identifying the Mobile Node and Its Service
sections.content:
The Mobile-Node-Identifier attribute, of type value 145, is of type String and contains the mobile node identifier in the form of a Network Access Identifier. This identifier and the identifier used for access authentication may be different, but there needs to be a mapping between the two identities as specified in the Proxy Mobile IPv6 specification. The attribute is used on the interface between the mobile access gateway and the AAA server, and is designed for deployments where the identity used during network access authentication and the identity used for mobility management are decoupled. It may also be the case that the gateway has no means of finding out the mobile node identity that could be used in subsequent Proxy Binding Update and Proxy Binding Acknowledgement exchanges, for example because of identity hiding during the network access authentication, or when the home AAA server wants to assign periodically changing identities to the mobile node. The attribute MAY be returned by the home AAA server in the RADIUS Access-Accept message, and the gateway MUST use the received identifier.

The Service-Selection attribute, of type value 146, is of type UTF-8 text and contains the name of the service or the external network with which the mobility service for the particular mobile node SHOULD be associated. The identifier MUST be unique within the Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain when normalized using the selected normalization form for that deployment. The gateway MUST include the attribute in the Access-Request sent to the AAA server if the information was acquired, for example by operator-specific configuration. The AAA server MAY include it in the Access-Accept even if it was not in the request, as a way of indicating the mobile node's default service. The Service Selection mobility option can be used in Proxy Binding Update and Acknowledgement messages between the gateway and the anchor; on the anchor-to-AAA interface the anchor MAY populate the attribute using the service information found in a received Proxy Binding Update, if such an option was included.
sections.plainLanguage: Two attributes name things. One gives the mobile node an identity for the mobility session, which may be deliberately different from the one used to sign in. The other names the service the session should belong to.

sections.title: Addresses, Prefixes and Servers
sections.content:
A group of attributes carries the addresses and the servers involved in the session. Each of them has a home variant and a visited variant, so the home network and the visited network can each be named separately.

The PMIP6-Home-LMA-IPv6-Address attribute, of type value 147, is of type IPv6 address and delivers the IPv6 address of the anchor located in the home network, which the gateway needs before it can initiate Proxy Mobile IPv6 signalling. The PMIP6-Visited-LMA-IPv6-Address attribute, of type value 148, does the same for an anchor in the visited network. PMIP6-Home-LMA-IPv4-Address, of type value 149, and PMIP6-Visited-LMA-IPv4-Address, of type value 150, are the IPv4 equivalents.

The PMIP6-Home-HN-Prefix and PMIP6-Visited-HN-Prefix attributes, of type values 151 and 152, carry the home network prefix, which is the prefix used by the mobile node in its home network. The PMIP6-Home-Interface-ID and PMIP6-Visited-Interface-ID attributes, of type values 153 and 154, carry the interface identifier used to form the mobile node's address. The PMIP6-Home-IPv4-HoA and PMIP6-Visited-IPv4-HoA attributes, of type values 155 and 156, carry the IPv4 home address.

Four attributes give the addresses of the DHCP servers to use: PMIP6-Home-DHCP4-Server-Address and PMIP6-Visited-DHCP4-Server-Address, of type values 157 and 158, and PMIP6-Home-DHCP6-Server-Address and PMIP6-Visited-DHCP6-Server-Address, of type values 159 and 160. Two more give the IPv4 gateways: PMIP6-Home-IPv4-Gateway and PMIP6-Visited-IPv4-Gateway, of type values 161 and 162.

The Calling-Station-Id attribute, of type value 31, and the Chargeable-User-Identity attribute, of type value 89, carry the identifiers of the calling station and of the user to be charged.
sections.plainLanguage: The gateway has to be told where the anchor is, which prefix the subscriber's address should use, and which address and DHCP servers to hand out. Each of those has a home version and a visited version, because the two networks may answer differently.

sections.title: The Mobile Access Gateway Interface
sections.content:
The interface from the mobile access gateway to the AAA RADIUS server is used for retrieval of the policy profile when a mobile node tries to attach, authenticate and authorize to a Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain. Depending on the policies and network capabilities, the gateway may retrieve different sets of session-related parameters: configuration attributes for the home or visited network access scenario depending on the location and attachment point of the mobile node; the IPv6 or IPv4 address of the designated anchor depending on the access network's actual IP topology; the IPv6 or IPv4 configuration parameters for the mobile node depending on the IP configuration method used and the individual mobile node's service policy; and the DHCP relay support attributes, IPv4 or IPv6, where that functionality is supported. In addition to these Proxy Mobile IPv6 specific attributes, other RADIUS attributes are used on the interface.

The User-Name attribute MUST be present in the Access-Request. It MUST carry a correctly formed identifier that SHOULD correspond to a mobile node identity unless the identity is being suppressed for policy reasons, such as when identity hiding is in effect. The mobile node identity, if available, MUST be in Network Access Identifier format. At minimum, the home realm of the mobile node MUST be available at the gateway when the network access authentication takes place, otherwise the gateway is not able to route RADIUS request messages towards the correct home AAA server. The identity used on this interface MAY be entirely related to the network access authentication and therefore not suitable as the mobile node identifier in subsequent Proxy Binding Update and Acknowledgement messages, in which case the home AAA server MUST provide the identifier using the Mobile-Node-Identifier attribute.

At least one of the NAS-IP-Address, NAS-IPv6-Address or NAS-Identifier attributes MUST be present in the Access-Request. The Service-Type attribute SHOULD be set to value 1, Login, and the NAS-Port-Type attribute SHOULD be present.

Accounting at the gateway follows RADIUS Accounting. The interface MUST support the transfer of accounting records that should include the time of binding cache entry creation and deletion and the number of octets sent and received by the mobile node over the bidirectional tunnel. If there is data traffic between a visiting mobile node and a correspondent node that is locally attached to an access link connected to the same gateway, the gateway MAY optimize the delivery effort by locally routing the packets instead of using reverse tunnelling to the mobile node's anchor. In that case the local data traffic too MUST be reported to the AAA accounting servers by means of RADIUS.
sections.plainLanguage: When the subscriber attaches, the gateway tells the home network who it is and what it can do, and gets back the profile: where the anchor is, which addresses to use, and what the policy allows. If the gateway routes traffic locally instead of tunnelling it back, it still has to report that traffic to the billing system.

sections.title: The Local Mobility Anchor Interface
sections.content:
The interface from the anchor to the home AAA server may be used for multiple purposes: authorization of the incoming Proxy Binding Update, updating the anchor address to the home AAA server, delegating the assignment of the home network prefix or the IPv4 home address to the home AAA server, and accounting and session management. The primary purpose is to update the home AAA server with the anchor address information in case of a dynamically assigned anchor, and to exchange the mobile node address assignment information between the anchor and the home AAA server.

Whenever the anchor sends an Access-Request, the User-Name attribute SHOULD contain the mobile node's identity, and it is strongly recommended to be the same as the identity in the mobile node identifier option of the Proxy Binding Update. The identity SHOULD also be the same as used on the gateway-to-home-AAA interface, but where those identities differ the home AAA server MUST have a mechanism for mapping one to the other. If the Proxy Binding Update contains the mobile node link-layer identifier option, the Calling-Station-Id attribute SHOULD be included, and if it contains the Service Selection mobility option, the Service-Selection attribute SHOULD be included. Both give the home AAA server more information for the authorization step.

The Service-Type attribute MUST be set to the value 17, Authorize Only. If the home AAA server is not able to authorize the subscriber's mobility service session, the Access-Reject message to the anchor MAY contain the Reply-Message attribute describing the reason, and the failure obviously results in a rejection of the Proxy Binding Update, with a Proxy Binding Acknowledgement carrying an appropriate error status value sent back to the gateway. The authorization step MUST be performed at least for the initial Proxy Binding Update that establishes the mobility session, and MAY be repeated for subsequent re-registration and handover, in which case the interface should also maintain an authorization session state.

In the case of dynamic anchor discovery and assignment, the home AAA server and the remote policy store may need to be updated with the selected anchor address information, which can be done during the Proxy Binding Update authorization step. The LMA address information in the request message MUST contain the IP address of the anchor, the Fully Qualified Domain Name that uniquely identifies it, or both, and refers to the Proxy Mobile IPv6 part of the anchor rather than the part that interfaces with the AAA infrastructure.

The anchor and the home AAA server use the home and visited home network prefix attributes to exchange the mobile node's prefix when appropriate, and the home and visited IPv4 home address attributes to exchange the IPv4 home address when appropriate. Which entity is actually responsible for address management is deployment specific within the Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain and MUST be pre-agreed per deployment. When the anchor is responsible, the prefix and address attributes inform the home AAA server and the remote policy store of what was assigned. It is also possible that the anchor delegates address management to the home AAA server, in which case the prefix and address are set to undefined addresses in the Access-Request and the anchor expects to receive the assigned values in the Access-Accept.

Accounting at the anchor follows RADIUS Accounting. The interface MUST support the transfer of the accounting records needed for service control and charging, including the time of binding cache entry creation and deletion and the number of octets sent and received by the mobile node over the bidirectional tunnel.
sections.plainLanguage: When the gateway asks the anchor to take the session, the anchor checks with the home network before accepting. The check is an authorize-only RADIUS request that carries the subscriber's identity and any addresses already assigned, and the answer says yes or no with a reason.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RADIUS messages may be transported between the gateway or the anchor and the RADIUS server via one or more AAA brokers or RADIUS proxies. In that case the communication between the anchor and the RADIUS AAA server relies on the security properties of the intermediate brokers and proxies.

Regarding the privacy threats associated with sending mobile node specific information between the gateway and the AAA server and between the anchor and the AAA server, the considerations of the RADIUS base protocol, RADIUS Accounting and the RADIUS EAP application are applicable. The gateway, the anchor and the AAA server SHOULD avoid including attributes containing personally identifying information such as the mobile node's interface identifier, link-layer address or Network Access Identifier, except as needed, and SHOULD pay special attention if identity hiding is desired.
sections.plainLanguage: Some of the attributes name the subscriber or their device, so they should be left out unless they are really needed. Where the messages cross a proxy, the security of the whole path rests on the proxy as well as on the ends.

messages.label: Access-Request
messages.note: Carries the User-Name, the NAS identifiers and the MIP6-Feature-Vector.

messages.label: Access-Accept
messages.note: Returns the policy profile: anchor addresses, home network prefix and the feature vector.

messages.label: Access-Request (Authorize Only)
messages.note: Carries the mobile node identity and the address information to be authorised.

items.title: Both in the home network
items.text: The gateway and the anchor both talk straight to the home AAA server.

items.title: Both in the visited network
items.text: The visited AAA server acts as a proxy towards the home AAA server and may add local policy.

items.title: Visited gateway, home anchor
items.text: The gateway reaches the home AAA server through the visited proxy, while the anchor has direct access.

items.label: PMIP6_SUPPORTED
items.desc: Proxy Mobile IPv6 mobility is supported and authorized.

items.label: IP4_HOA_SUPPORTED
items.desc: An IPv4 home address may be assigned as well as IPv6.

items.label: LOCAL_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED
items.desc: The gateway may route traffic locally instead of tunnelling it back.

items.label: IP4_TRANSPORT_SUPPORTED
items.desc: The gateway can carry IP traffic to the anchor over IPv4.

items.label: IP4_HOA_ONLY_SUPPORTED
items.desc: Only IPv4 mobility is authorized, so no IPv6 home network prefix is sent.
